lines.text: "Welcome back."
"Hm. This place is more crowded than before."
"Business has been better lately."
"Thanks to a certain critic, maybe."
"Well, popularity raises expectations too."
"…Right."
"So? Same confidence as usual, or are you here to actually enjoy the food today?"
"Depends. I heard your Cơm Tấm is getting talked about."
"Then let’s see if the line outside makes sense."
"The ribs have a nice lacquer on the surface."
"There’s a caramel shine around the edges, like the marinade reduced properly."
"The rice looks separated too. Not mushy, not clumped into one block."
"Each grain still keeps its shape, which is a good sign for a broken-rice plate."
"Visually, it has promise. The plate knows how to sell itself."
"Heh. That sounds like a compliment."
"For now, it is."
"The rib gives me more resistance than I expected."
"When I press in, it doesn’t break cleanly. It pulls back first."
"That kind of bite can work if it feels intentional."
"Here, it starts to feel like the meat is making me do extra work."
"The rice sounds fine though. Light, separate, not wet and heavy."
"So the base is okay. The rib is where I’m starting to question it."
"Alright, I think I’ve got the plate now."
"The ribs carry a nice caramel layer and a deeper grilled note."
"The rice has that broken-grain texture, loose enough to feel proper."
"It isn’t dry either; there’s still enough warmth and softness to carry the sauce."
"But the rib fights back too much."
"The plate has good ideas, but the main bite doesn’t land as cleanly as it should."
"That should be enough for the report."
"So?"
"How’s the Cơm Tấm?"
"The rice texture was fine."
"The broken grains stayed separate, and the sauce didn’t drown them."
"The rib had good glaze and a strong grilled depth."
"But it was too resistant for what the plate needed."
"I actually changed the recipe a little…"
"And honestly? I don’t really understand why people line up for this."
"…That harsh, huh?"
"I’m just being honest."
"That report feels off."
"You sure you looked at the whole plate?"
"The rice, the rib, and the sauce don’t all say the same thing."
"If you only judge the glaze, you’ll miss what happens when you actually press into it."
"Right. I should check the surface, the rice, and the bite again."
"The answer should come from how it looks and how it breaks down."
